ideas.name: Ethiopia's CRGE strategy and its four pillars

en.text: Ethiopia's Climate Resilient Green Economy (CRGE) strategy follows a green growth path that fosters development and sustainability. It takes a sectoral approach and first prioritized 60 initiatives to reach development goals with fewer GHG emissions. Its four pillars: improving crop and livestock practices for income and food security while cutting emissions; protecting and re-establishing forests and their carbon stocks; expanding renewable electricity for home and regional markets; and leapfrogging to modern, energy-efficient technologies in transport, industry and buildings. It aims to protect Ethiopia from climate change and help it reach middle-income status by 2025.

en.text: Electricity powers cities, industry and irrigation pumps, and Ethiopia needs to expand its supply about 14 % per year. It plans to use its vast hydro, geothermal, solar and wind potential, which gives electricity at virtually zero GHG emissions and may produce a surplus to export to neighbouring countries. In transport and industries such as cement, textile, leather and fertilizer, the CRGE promotes energy efficiency, alternative fuels, stricter fuel-efficiency standards and an electric rail network powered by renewable energy, leapfrogging older polluting technology.
